articles.title: 103-year-old D-Day veteran receives replacement medals 80 years after returning his uniform
articles.description: Douglas Halley, a 103-year-old D-Day veteran, recently received his wartime medals which were lost in 1945. A young historian, Joseph Smith, discovered Halley's military record while researching veterans' stories and assisted in recovering the medals. The Ministry of Defence located and mailed the medals back to Halley just before Remembrance Day. This story highlights the importance of remembering personal histories and the sacrifices of war.

articles.title: Man finds centuries-old gold ring after 15 minutes of metal detecting
articles.description: Kevin Short found a centuries-old gold ring inscribed “I live in hope” just 15 minutes into a metal-detecting search in Warwickshire. Authenticated by the British Museum, the 16th-to-18th-century ring is expected to fetch up to £3,000 at a December 2 auction.

Over 28 cyclists carry Thanksgiving turkeys on their bikes in Maine; unusual ride helps 58 families get free holiday dinners
articles.description: More than 28 cyclists participated in the eighth annual Turkey Ride to deliver Thanksgiving turkeys. They gathered at Maine Sport Rockport and picked up items from Hannaford Supermarkets. After collecting donations, they transported the groceries to the Camden Area Christian Food Pantry. Fifty-eight families benefited from the food pantry's effort, receiving turkeys for their Thanksgiving meals. The event highlighted community support for those in need and encouraged charitable involvement.

articles.title: Debt, dues and deja vu: How poor nations end up paying more than they borrow
articles.description: In 2025, low and middle-income countries are grappling with an alarming spike in external debt, hitting a staggering $9.4 trillion. Alongside this, debt repayment burdens surged to $1.4 trillion, largely due to escalating borrowing rates and a scarcity of new financial support. Nations receiving IDA funding are particularly strained, facing average interest rates of 8.2 percent.

articles.title: AI agents could help banks generate nearly 3x returns over three years: McKinsey
articles.description: Banks are considering adopting artificial intelligence agents, expecting to recover investments within around ten months. Analysis suggests substantial returns of nearly three times the initial investment over three years. Increasing competition emphasizes the need for banks to move quickly beyond pilot projects for effective integration. However, productivity gains from AI do not guarantee improved profits for banks, indicating a gap in performance.

articles.title: Rupee rises 6 paise to 94.13 as crude oil prices ease, strong dollar limit gains
articles.description: The rupee bounced back, gaining 6 paise to reach 94.13 against the US dollar during early trading hours. This recovery was aided by declining crude oil prices and a rise in local equities. Despite a previous setback of 7 paise, external pressures from a stronger dollar and rising US Treasury yields remained. Notably, foreign institutional investors brought confidence to the market with equities worth Rs 5,736.

articles.title: Indian bonds brace for a rough week as US treasury selloff sends yields soaring
articles.description: At the onset of the week, Indian government bonds are likely to encounter significant pressure stemming from the rise in US yields. The noticeable increase in the US 10-year Treasury yield has shifted market sentiments regarding possible changes in monetary policy. Furthermore, with domestic retail inflation surging to 6.09%, which is above the Reserve Bank of India's target, concerns about imminent interest rate hikes in December are becoming prevalent.

articles.title: Is AI widening the gender gap at work? Pew Research finds women's employment growth lagging behind men's in AI-exposed jobs
articles.description: A Pew Research Center analysis has highlighted an emerging gender divide in the US labour market, with women's employment growth lagging behind men's in occupations more exposed to artificial intelligence. The findings reveal sharper disparities among workers without bachelor's degrees, raising concerns about automation, occupational inequality and women's future employment prospects.

articles.title: INSPIRE-SHE scholarship 2026: Government invites applications for 12,000 students; check eligibility and benefits
articles.description: Eligible students are invited to apply for the INSPIRE Scholarship for Higher Education through the official website. Applications will be accepted from November 7, 2026, to December 7, 2026, specifically for meritorious students. Selected candidates will receive financial support, including a monthly scholarship and a mentorship grant during the final years. The scholarship is available for various basic and natural science courses at recognized institutions.

articles.title: US universities oppose proposed $70,000 OPT fee: Could Indian students lose post-study work opportunities?
articles.description: The US Department of Homeland Security has proposed a $70,000 fee for an initial Optional Practical Training recommendation and $30,000 for subsequent recommendations for an international student. The fee would be payable by the institution recommending OPT, not directly by the student under the proposal. The American Council on Education and 36 higher education organisations have urged the government to withdraw the plan.

articles.title: New Zealand extends post-study work visa to four years for Indian PhD graduates from today; check details here
articles.description: New Zealand will extend post-study work visa eligibility to up to four years for Indian PhD graduates from November 16, 2026, under the India–New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA). The agreement also provides up to two years for bachelor's graduates and three years for master's graduates, subject to eligibility requirements. Indian students will also be guaranteed at least 20 hours of weekly in-study work rights, alongside new employment and mobility opportunities for Indian professionals.

articles.title: Gracie Abrams to tour in Australia next year
articles.description: Gracie Abrams has officially confirmed her upcoming tour in Australia for the year 2027, featuring six performances. She will perform three shows at Melbourne's Rod Laver Arena and three at Sydney’s Afterpay Arena. British singer-songwriter Arlo Parks will open for her during all performances. Fans can sign up for early access to ticket sales starting November 18 and general sale on November 20.
